intro.lede: Two writing systems that solved the same problem in opposite directions. Hebrew writes the consonants and leaves the vowels to the reader. Devanagari builds every syllable as a single unit and hangs it from a line. Neither is harder than the other. They are differently shaped.
intro.note: This page is a reference for a reader starting from zero in either script. It teaches the shapes and the logic. It does not teach the languages, and it does not pretend that learning a script is the same as learning a language.

structure.hebrew: An abjad. The letters are consonants. Vowels are normally not written at all, and a fluent reader supplies them from context.
structure.hindi: An abugida, sometimes called an alphasyllabary. Every consonant carries a built in 'a' sound, and other vowels are written as marks attached to it.

structure.hebrew: Right to left. Numbers inside Hebrew text still run left to right, which is why mixed text needs care.
22 letters. Five of them take a different final form when they end a word.
structure.hindi: Traditionally 11 to 13 vowels and 33 consonants, arranged by where in the mouth the sound is made.

structure.hebrew: A square script that sits on the line, dense and blocky, with most letters the same height.
structure.hindi: A horizontal head line, the shirorekha, runs across the top and joins the letters of a word into one connected strip.

structure.hebrew: Niqqud, a system of dots and dashes above and below the letters, exists but is used mainly in prayer books, poetry, dictionaries and books for children and learners.
structure.hindi: Matras, vowel marks attached to a consonant. These are always written, so a Devanagari text is fully vocalised as a matter of course.
Written as conjuncts, where two or more consonant shapes fuse into one new shape. This is the part that takes longest to learn.

structure.hebrew: Every letter has a numeric value, from alef as 1 to tav as 400. The practice of reading words as numbers is called gematria.
structure.hindi: Devanagari has its own digits, 0 to 9. Separately, the katapayadi system used in Sanskrit mathematics and astronomy encoded numbers as letters, which allowed formulae to be memorised as verse.

structure.hebrew: Hebrew is the official language of the State of Israel. It is the only case of a language returning from liturgical and literary use to full everyday spoken use across a whole society.
structure.hindi: Under Article 343 of the Constitution of India, Hindi in the Devanagari script is the official language of the Union, with English as an associate official language. Devanagari is also used for Marathi, Nepali, Konkani and Sanskrit among others.

structure.hebrew: The Hebrew script is also used to write Yiddish, Ladino and Judeo Arabic. Bene Israel and Cochin Jewish communities in India encountered it primarily as a liturgical script.
structure.hindi: Devanagari is one of many Indian scripts. The Cochin Jewish community lived in a Malayalam speaking region, and the Bene Israel in a Marathi speaking one, which is a reminder that 'Indian script' is never a single thing.

hebrewLetters.name: Alef
hebrewLetters.note: Carries a vowel rather than a sound of its own.

hebrewLetters.name: Bet
hebrewLetters.note: A dot inside, the dagesh, makes it hard: b.

hebrewLetters.name: He
hebrewLetters.note: Often silent at the end of a word.

hebrewLetters.name: Chet
hebrewLetters.note: A back of the throat sound with no English equivalent.

hebrewLetters.name: Lamed
hebrewLetters.note: The only letter that rises above the line.

hebrewLetters.name: Ayin
hebrewLetters.note: Like alef, mainly a vowel carrier in modern speech.

hebrewLetters.name: Shin
hebrewLetters.note: The dot on the right gives sh, on the left gives s.

devanagariVowels.note: Built into every consonant by default.
The mark is written before the consonant but read after it.

devanagariNote: The consonant grid is not alphabetical in the European sense. It is a map of the mouth. Each row moves the point of contact further forward, from the throat to the lips, and within each row the sounds move from unvoiced to voiced to nasal. Once that is seen, the order stops being a list to memorise and becomes a diagram.

phrases.meaning: Peace, and also hello and goodbye
phrases.note: Shalom is built on the root for wholeness. Namaste is a greeting of respect rather than a word for peace. The two are used in the same slot in conversation but mean different things.
The Hindi word arrives through Persian and Arabic, which is a reminder that both languages sit inside larger borrowing networks.
